title: 50 storey residential tower, Brisbane CBD: electrical
workplace: 50 storey residential tower with foyer and 3 level basement carpark, Brisbane CBD
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the contractor's own procedures and the project's documents.

swms.title: Construction power and temporary lighting
swms.task: Install, test and maintain construction power and temporary lighting for the tower, the foyer and the 3 level basement carpark: site switchboards, distribution boards, leads and lighting, connected to the energised builder's supply.

facts.constructionTesting: The site electrician inspects and tests construction wiring, switchboards and RCDs, and leads are tested and tagged, at the intervals AS/NZS 3012 sets, recorded in the site register.
facts.isolationProcedure: Circuits are isolated at the site switchboard, locked with each worker's personal lock and a danger tag, and tested de-energised by the licensed electrician before work.
facts.fallControl: Lighting and leads in risers, stairs and shafts are installed from platforms with guardrails, and riser openings are screened.

steps: Install construction power and temporary lighting
Inspect, test and maintain construction power
Work on or near energised parts
missing: Work on or near energised parts
Inspection and testing of construction wiring

swms.title: Cast-in conduits on the deck
swms.task: Install cast-in conduits and in-slab electrical services on the deck of each post-tensioned floor before the pour, alongside the formwork and reo crews. Work is near the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.fallControl: Work is done inside the perimeter screens and edge protection, with penetrations covered.

steps: Install cast-in conduits on the deck before the pour

swms.title: Cable tray, containment and cabling at height
swms.task: Install cable tray, containment and cabling in the risers, the apartment ceilings, the double height foyer and the 3 level basement carpark, working from elevating work platforms and ladders, more than 2 m above the floor.

facts.fallControl: Elevating work platforms with guardrails are used for work above 2 m, risers are screened at each level, and only the section being worked on is opened and fenced.

steps: Install cable tray, containment and cabling at height

swms.title: Cable pulling and cable drums
swms.task: Pull sub-main and final subcircuit cables up the risers and through the basement carpark, with cable drums lifted to the floors by the tower crane and moved on the floor with a forklift. Work at the open risers is more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.craneCompany: The tower cranes are supplied and operated by the crane company, Example Cranes Pty Ltd, under its lift plans.
facts.loadLimits: Cable drums are landed and stored within the slab loads on the builder's load plan, signed at each landing area.
facts.fallControl: Risers are screened at each level, and cables are pulled from inside the screens with only the section being worked on opened and fenced.

steps: Plan lifts with the crane company
Work with the crane crew during lifts
Pull cables and handle cable drums

swms.title: Apartment rough-in and fit-off
swms.task: Rough-in and fit-off the electrical installation in the apartments: chase and drill walls, run cables in the ceiling spaces, and fit power points, switches and light fittings, working from platform ladders.

facts.isolationProcedure: Each circuit is isolated at the distribution board, locked with a personal lock and danger tag, and tested de-energised by a licensed electrician before work.
facts.silicaControls: Chasing and drilling are done with on-tool dust extraction, with fit tested P2 respirators, and the written silica assessment is done before work starts.

steps: Work on or near energised parts
missing: Work on or near energised parts

swms.title: Main switchboards, terminations, energising and commissioning
swms.task: Install the main switchboard, distribution boards and consumer mains in the basement switchroom and on each floor, terminate the cables, then test, energise and commission the installation with the distribution entity.

facts.isolationProcedure: Each circuit is isolated at its switchboard, locked with each worker's personal lock and a danger tag, and tested de-energised by a licensed electrician using a proved tester before work.
